description: Performance fixture for embed-dedup insert path. Pins the deterministic decision-count + embedder-call shape that the live no-mock e2e in tests/embed_dedup_e2e.rs emits as ee.test_event.v1 events. Concrete latency numbers are intentionally NOT pinned — they vary by host class. The fixture pins the COUNTS and SHAPE so a regression that silently disables dedup or burns extra embeddings trips the contract.

scenarios.name: disabled_default_workspace_identical_burst
scenarios.intent: When embed-dedup is disabled, identical-content inserts must not invoke any dedup decision path; both inserts run the embedder.

scenarios.name: enabled_workspace_identical_burst
scenarios.intent: When embed-dedup is enabled with hammingK=12 / cosineFloor=0.97, an identical-content second insert must reuse exactly the first memory's embedding without invoking the embedder again.

scenarios.name: enabled_workspace_typo_near_duplicate
scenarios.intent: Near-duplicate content with both SimHash hamming distance below cap AND cosine similarity above floor must reuse. If either gate fails it must NOT reuse.

scenarios.name: strict_workspace_simhash_collision_rejected
scenarios.intent: With cosineFloor=1.0 the cosine gate rejects any near-duplicate even when SimHash hamming distance is within cap, proving the second gate prevents false-positive collisions from corrupting reuse decisions.

scenarios.name: feature_disabled_preserves_legacy_pack_search
scenarios.intent: When embed-dedup is disabled the pack/search output must remain byte-identical to the pre-feature baseline. No dedupLink in why/audit, no degraded codes from the feature path.

scenarios.name: stale_simhash_index_degrades_honestly
scenarios.intent: When the SimHash index is missing or stale, inserts must degrade honestly: dedup decision is skipped, a degraded code is emitted, and no memory is lost.

notes: writeLatencyDeltaMs bounds are intentionally permissive (null or wide-range) because absolute timing is host-dependent; the fixture pins counts and decision shape, not wall-clock latency.

embedderCallCount is the number of times the embedder was invoked across the scenario's insert sequence. embedderCallsAvoidedVsLegacy is the count saved vs the disabled-baseline scenario for the same insert sequence.

expectedDegradedCodes lists the exact set of degraded codes the scenario expects in the response envelope. Empty array means the response must carry no degraded entries from the embed-dedup feature path.
